article.title: Tesla in 10 Charts: How the Business Works, Visualized (2026)
breadcrumb: Tesla in 10 Charts: How the Business Works, Visualized (2026)
article.author: Daniel Pereira

segments.name: Automotive + Services/Other
segments.notes: Vehicles and related services; the core business.

segments.name: Energy Generation & Storage
segments.notes: Grew in 2025 mainly due to higher Megapack and Powerwall deployments; growth pillar.

revenue_2025.footer_takeaway: Tesla remains automotive-led today, but energy is becoming an increasingly important growth pillar.

business_model_snapshot.subtitle: How Tesla connects vehicles, software, energy, infrastructure, and customer relationships.

nodes.label: Vehicle Sales & Leasing
nodes.detail: EV sales, leasing, used vehicles, and automotive services.

nodes.label: Energy Products
nodes.detail: Powerwall, Megapack, solar, and storage solutions.

nodes.label: Services & Extras
nodes.detail: Paid Supercharging, insurance, maintenance, parts, merchandise, and software features.

nodes.label: Direct Customer Relationship
nodes.detail: Website, app, stores, and delivery centers; more control over pricing and experience.

nodes.label: Strategic Assets
nodes.detail: Brand, factories, battery technology, software, charging network, and vehicle data.

nodes.label: Key Takeaway
nodes.detail: Tesla combines vehicles, software, energy, infrastructure, and direct customer relationships.

loop_steps: Strong brand awareness creates demand for vehicles
More vehicle sales increase cars on the road
More cars generate more customer data, software feedback, charging usage, service interactions
Insights improve software, customer experience, ecosystem
Supercharger network, over-the-air updates, software features increase customer loyalty
Customer loyalty strengthens brand and supports future demand

weaknesses: Challenge of scaling service capacity as fleet grows

social: Shift toward sustainability and electric mobility
Brand perception affected by public controversy

competitor_groups: Traditional car manufacturers transitioning to electric
competitive_landscape.notes: Competition intensified, especially in lower-cost EVs and in China, where BYD has become a major force.

segments: Megapack utility and commercial storage customers

risks: Competition from Chinese and legacy automakers

future_growth_map.key_question: Whether Tesla can transform from an EV manufacturer into a broader technology and energy platform.

conclusion.one_sentence: Tesla is an automotive-led company trying to become a broader technology and energy platform.
challenges_summary: Difficulty turning long-term bets into profitable businesses
